revision: S1 placement (10HP; THT + the vertical USB-C, the board-to-board strips, the power and SWD headers and BOOT/RESET only). Two boards: carrier (jack board, 4 layers) and MCU board (4 layers) stacked on the carrier F side on 2.54 mm strips, as modules/usb-audio. Every other SMD part parked off-board for group-by-group placement. Not routed. 2026-11-08: + two M3x10 F-F hex standoffs MS1/MS2 beside the MCU board (mount_standoffs), coaxial panel holes H20/H21.
frame: Panel frame: origin at the panel upper-left corner seen from the front, X across (right), Y down, mm. KiCad sheet position = kicad_origin + panel XY, for the carrier, the MCU board and the panel. The carrier F side faces the panel; the MCU board sits on the carrier F side with its own F side facing the panel, so both KiCad top views equal the front view (no mirroring).
rail_note: Doepfer A-100 10HP: 50.5 mm wide; holes X7.5 and X7.5 + 7 x 5.08 (Doepfer (HP - 3) x 5.08 spacing, as modules/acid 8HP and modules/4mix 18HP), the left one moved 1HP right to X12.58 so both land on the 2HP case spacer grid (case/tools/build_case.py). Skiff rails: clear Y8.0..120.5.
hp_decision: 10HP (user 2026-11-06: 8HP preferred, 10HP if needed; no schematic changes). Fit study in docs/research.md section 5: at 8HP the jack columns leave 5.55 mm strips, so no SOIC-14 / SOT-223 / codec fits in the jack area and all of them crowd the 31 mm band under the MCU board; SMD courtyard / free area 65 % against 45 % (usb-audio) .. 53 % (16bit) .. 63 % (32bit, needed hand-solder exceptions) on the routed boards. At 10HP the strips are 11.15 mm (a SOIC-14 plus a 0603 column) and the density is 45 %. Moving parts to the MCU board would need new strip pins, i.e. a schematic change on both boards.

main_pcb.note: 49.5 x 110.0 mm, 0.5 mm inside the 50.5 mm panel each side and 1.25 mm inside the rail gap at each end (as modules/acid). Held by the 14 jack nuts; the MCU board hangs on it. All SMD on B (single-sided assembly).

mcu_pcb.note: 29.0 x 29.55 mm: the modules/usb-audio MCU board outline (R1/R2) and strip/USB-C positions, centred on the panel (X + 10.25), so its proven USB 2.0 HS layout can be carried over. All SMD on F (one assembly side), facing the panel.

stack_Z_mm.datum: Z0 = carrier F.Cu, +Z toward the panel
stack_Z_mm.note: PJ301M-12 boss top = panel rear (as modules/usb-audio).
stack_Z_mm.usbc_note: As modules/usb-audio: the USB-C mouth must be no more than ~0.3 mm behind the panel front or the plug cannot seat; HRO TYPE-C-31-D-15 (8.8 mm) on a 1.6 mm MCU board on 2.5 mm header plastic puts it 1.3 mm proud of the 1.6 mm FR4 panel.

layout_note: User brief 2026-11-06: USB-C at the top (as modules/usb-audio); three columns, IN 1-6 in two rows of three, OUT 1-8 in three rows below, reading order (left to right, top to bottom); the ninth spot (bottom right) is empty on the panel and holds the power header on the back. Columns X7.0 / X25.25 / X43.5 (7.0 mm from both panel edges, 18.25 mm pitch): jack courtyards 1.72 mm from the carrier edges; with the 2 mm hand-solder keep-out (pads + 2 mm, X +/-3.55) the strips between the columns are 11.15 mm wide (X10.55..21.7, X28.8..39.95). Rows Y46.3 / 62.25 / 78.2 / 94.15 / 110.1 (15.95 mm pitch): the top row courtyard (Y40.02) clears the MCU board (Y39.55); the bottom row courtyard (Y117.93) is 1.3 mm from the carrier edge.

usb_slot.note: Obround NPTH slot for the receptacle shell (8.94 x 3.16 mm) with ~0.27 mm clearance a side, as modules/usb-audio; the shell passes through and stands 1.3 mm proud.

reserved_zones_mcu.what: U101 LQFP-64 (modules/usb-audio R2 spot: centre X25.25 Y31.75)

back_side_parts.band: Eurorack power in the empty ninth jack spot (bottom right), vertical, pin 1 (-12 V) at the bottom row. THT, B side
SWD (WCH-LinkE): pin 1 +3V3 at the top, B side, top-left beside J2 (SWDIO/SWCLK on J2.3/J2.4); tails on F clear of the MCU board
RESET, B side, below J4 (NRST on J2.5)
BOOT, B side, below RESET (BOOT0 on J2.6)

power_header.idc_note: A 16-pin cable plugs on aligned at pin 1 (red stripe = -12 V, at the bottom); positions 11-16 overhang upward over the OUT6 jack tails, 2.5 mm above B (SMD under it must stay below 2.5 mm).

mount_standoffs.hardware: per standoff: 1 x M3 F-F hex standoff 10 mm, 2 x M3x6 pan/button head (ISO 7380), as modules/4mix. Not M3x8: two M3x8 would meet inside a through-tapped 10 mm standoff.
mount_standoffs.note: User 2026-11-08: two M3 hex standoffs at the top beside the USB-C port so pushing the plug does not move the carrier (modules/usb-audio needed a printed brace); the first try beside the strips at Y35.4 was rejected (user: on the top, around the USB port). Carrier F to panel rear is 10 mm (stack_Z_mm), so each standoff is coaxial: carrier hole = panel hole. Mirror images about the panel centre X25.25 at the top corners, level with the USB-C (Y16) and as high / far out as the 1 mm edge keep-out allows (courtyards 1.00 mm from the edge): the hex (corners R3.18) clears the MCU board outline (X10.75..39.75) by >= 2.5 mm, the panel bolt heads (R2.75) sit between the rail band and the IN labels. No F copper inside R3.3 and no B copper inside R3.5; In1/In2 planes are cut by the NPTH only. Carrier footprints: board-only, empty Reference + MechanicalID MS1/MS2 (shared parity: mechanical), NPTH 3.2, F courtyard R3.3, B courtyard R3.4 (M3 head R2.85), 3D model standoff-m3x10.step from modules/4mix. Placed on the routed carrier by research/route/c_b30_standoffs_top.py: J4 SWD down 5.1, SW1/SW2 down, Y1 right 1.0 with C29 upright, C28 to the +3V3_C via by J2; buck core (L1 U2 C6 C7 C8 R3 R4 R5 R20) down 2.3 with its copper, C9/C10 left 0.5, C5 under C10, C4 left of L1, R13 upright by J3, FB2 below the core.
